Nested-quote check: " ' " ' "

Let

\[
\Delta T_s(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty=C\,x^{-1},
\]

with \(C\) constant and \(x\) measured along the vertical surface from the leading edge in the direction of the buoyancy-driven flow. Assume laminar natural convection, Boussinesq buoyancy, constant properties, quiescent ambient fluid, and no forced convection.

### Scaling

Let

\[
U(x)=u_{\max},\qquad V(x)=v(y\to\infty),\qquad \delta(x)=\text{boundary-layer thickness}.
\]

Momentum balance:

\[
\frac{U^2}{x}\sim g\beta \Delta T_s \sim x^{-1}
\]

so

\[
U\sim x^0.
\]

Thermal balance: the wall-temperature streamwise gradient is

\[
\frac{\partial T}{\partial x}\sim \frac{C}{x^2},
\]

while conduction normal to the wall is

\[
\alpha \frac{\Delta T_s}{\delta^2}\sim \frac{C}{x\,\delta^2}.
\]

Balancing,

\[
\frac{C}{x^2}\sim \frac{C}{x\,\delta^2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\delta\sim x^{1/2}.
\]

Continuity gives

\[
V\sim \frac{U\delta}{x}\sim x^{0+1/2-1}=x^{-1/2}.
\]

The local heat flux is

\[
q''\sim k\frac{\Delta T_s}{\delta}
\sim \frac{C}{x^{1/2+1}}
\sim x^{-3/2}.
\]

The heat rate per unit width, whether viewed as the heat content carried in the layer or as the integral of \(q''\), scales as

\[
Q\sim \Delta T_s\,V\,\delta
\sim x^{-1}\,x^{-1/2}\,x^{1/2}
\sim x^{-1/2}.
\]

If \(Q\) is defined as a cumulative heat transfer from a finite cutoff \(x_0\) to \(x\), it has the same \(x^{-1/2}\) dependence, up to an additive constant and sign convention. A formal integral from \(x=0\) is singular.

### Variation with \(x\)

\[
\boxed{q'' \propto x^{-3/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{Q \propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\delta \propto x^{1/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{u_{\max} \propto x^0}
\]

\[
\boxed{v_\infty \propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

More explicitly,

\[
u_{\max}\sim (g\beta C)^{1/2},
\]

\[
\delta\sim \left(\frac{\alpha x}{g\beta C}\right)^{1/2},
\]

\[
v_\infty\sim \left(\alpha g\beta C\right)^{1/2}x^{-1/2},
\]

up to Prandtl-number-dependent constants.

### Physical realizability

The exact law \(\Delta T_s\propto 1/x\) is singular at the leading edge:

\[
\Delta T_s\to\infty,\qquad
q''\to\infty,\qquad
Q\to\infty,\qquad
v_\infty\to\infty
\quad\text{as }x\to0.
\]

Moreover, the heat-flux singularity is not integrable:

\[
\int_0^x \xi^{-3/2}\,d\xi
\]

diverges. Therefore a finite physical heat source cannot generate this exact flow all the way to \(x=0\).

It is obtainable only in an idealized mathematical sense: as a singular similarity solution for \(x>0\), produced by a vertical surface whose temperature is prescribed as

\[
T_w-T_\infty=C/x
\]

and which is supplied with a heat-flux distribution

\[
q''\propto x^{-3/2},
\]

or equivalently by an idealized infinite line/point heat source at the leading edge. In a real experiment, one could approximate it only on a finite domain, say \(x\ge x_0>0\), or by actively imposing the \(1/x\) wall-temperature distribution away from the singular leading edge, while the flow remains laminar and below transition to turbulence.
